home.title: aria2t — Terminal Client for the aria2 Download Manager
home.description: A terminal UI for aria2: downloads, torrents, magnet links, and Metalink with a managed daemon, file selection, speed scheduling, and sha-256 integrity checks.
home.hero.lede: aria2t talks to aria2 over JSON-RPC: either to a private daemon it spawns and manages itself, or to any aria2 already running on a seedbox, NAS, or remote machine. Everything works with both the keyboard and the mouse, and the application builds into a single static Go binary.
home.feat.sources.title: Support for every aria2 source
home.feat.sources.body: URL mirrors, .torrent, .metalink, magnet links, and aria2 input files.
home.feat.nosetup.title: No-setup start
home.feat.nosetup.body: aria2t finds aria2c, spawns a private daemon, and manages its full lifecycle; an external aria2 connects through the --url flag.
home.feat.manage.title: Download management
home.feat.manage.body: Pause and resume one or all, remove, reorder the queue, and cap speeds per download or on a schedule.
home.feat.detail.title: Details for every download
home.feat.detail.body: Piece map, peer and mirror speeds, per-file progress, share ratio, and BitTorrent seeding controls.
home.feat.limits.title: Speed limits and scheduling
home.feat.limits.body: Per-download caps picked from presets, saved global caps, and a scheduler that changes the global limit by time of day.
home.feat.integrity.title: Integrity checking
home.feat.integrity.body: Finished files are compared against a sha-256 checksum and re-downloaded on mismatch; errors are described in plain language rather than error codes.
home.feat.persist.title: State preserved across restarts
home.feat.persist.body: Finished and in-progress downloads are restored, and a file-selection window closed without an answer opens again.
home.feat.mouse.title: Keyboard and mouse
home.feat.mouse.body: Every action is reachable both ways: the key-bar hints are clickable, and the full list of bindings opens with ?.
home.sources.body: Anything aria2 accepts can be added to aria2t: plain URLs (multiple lines are treated as mirrors of the same file), magnet links and .torrent files with DHT and seeding support, .metalink, and aria2's --input-file batch format with per-entry options.
home.how.body: Files are downloaded by an aria2 daemon; the interface controls it over JSON-RPC. By default aria2t finds aria2c on PATH and starts a private daemon on a random port with a random secret. The session is saved on exit and restored on the next launch; the child process stops cleanly with the program, and a daemon left behind by a crash is shut down on the next start.
home.engine.body: aria2t is a control panel for aria2. Pointed at an aria2 that is already running — on a seedbox, a NAS, or in a Docker container — it connects as a regular RPC client and the built-in daemon never starts. The application collects no analytics or telemetry; its only network traffic goes to the aria2 servers you configure.
home.start.body: Install aria2, get the aria2t binary, and add your first download — or connect to a server you already run.
home.faq.what.q: What is aria2 and why does it need a separate interface?
home.faq.what.a: aria2 is a fast download engine supporting HTTP(S), FTP, SFTP, BitTorrent, and Metalink. It runs in the background, is controlled over JSON-RPC, and has no interface of its own beyond one-off commands. aria2t adds a real-time download list, file selection, queue management, speed limits, and integrity checking.
home.faq.aria2c.q: How is this different from running aria2c directly?
home.faq.aria2c.a: aria2c either downloads a file and exits, or runs as a daemon controlled by scripts. aria2t takes over managing that daemon: it starts it, saves and restores the session, stops it cleanly on exit, and shuts down a daemon left behind by a crash. On top of that aria2t provides an interactive interface.
home.faq.external.q: Does it work with an aria2 I already run?
home.faq.external.a: Yes. The --url ws://host:6800/jsonrpc --secret … flag or the built-in server switcher with latency probes connects aria2t to any aria2 over WebSocket or HTTP(S) — for example on a seedbox, a NAS, or in a Docker container. The built-in daemon is not started in that case.
home.faq.persist.a: Yes. The managed daemon saves its session on exit and restores it on the next launch: active, waiting, finished, and seeding downloads are restored, and already-downloaded files are recognized rather than downloaded again. A file-selection window closed without an answer also opens again.
home.faq.files.q: Can I choose which files of a torrent to download?
home.faq.files.a: Yes. Torrents, magnet links, and Metalink are added paused, and a file tree opens first; a magnet link is paused after its metadata arrives. Data transfer starts only after the selection is confirmed, and it can be changed later with f.
home.faq.seed.a: Yes. A finished torrent keeps seeding and its status changes to seeding. The global seeding parameters — ratio and time — are set in the settings and re-applied on every daemon restart.
home.faq.mouse.a: Both are fully supported. Every hint in the key bar can be clicked, every mouse action has a keyboard equivalent, and the full list of bindings opens with ?.
home.faq.telemetry.q: Does aria2t send any data anywhere?
home.faq.telemetry.a: No. The program collects no analytics or telemetry, fetches no remote configuration, and talks over the network only to the aria2 server you configure.
install.title: Install aria2t — Terminal Client for aria2 (macOS, Linux)
install.description: Install guide for the aria2t terminal client: install aria2, download a release binary or build from source with Go, and connect to a local or remote aria2.
install.lede: aria2t is a single static binary; aria2 supplies the download engine. Three steps and the first download is running.
install.before.title: Before you start
install.before.aria2: aria2 — needed only for the built-in daemon; connecting to an external server does not require it.
install.before.terminal: A terminal with 256-color or true-color support. Mouse optional: everything can be done from the keyboard.
install.before.go: Go 1.25 or newer, only if you build from source.
install.step1.title: Step 1 — Install aria2
install.step1.body: The managed daemon runs your system's aria2c. Any recent version works.
install.step2.title: Step 2 — Get aria2t
install.step2.body1: Download the archive for your platform from GitHub Releases and put the binary on your PATH.
install.step3.title: Step 3 — First run
install.step3.body1: On first launch aria2t starts a private daemon and opens an empty download list. Press a to open the add form, or ↵ to add a link from the clipboard.
install.step3.body2: To connect to an already-running aria2 instead:
install.step3.body3: Configuration is stored in ~/.config/aria2t/config.json (override the path with --config); the managed daemon's session lives under ~/.config/aria2t/daemon/.
install.updating.title: Updating
install.updating.body: Replace the binary with a newer build. Configuration, scheduler rules, and the daemon session are kept under ~/.config/aria2t/ and survive the swap.
install.uninstalling.title: Uninstalling
privacy.title: Privacy — aria2t
privacy.description: What aria2t stores and where its network traffic goes: everything is local, no analytics or telemetry in the application, connections only to the aria2 servers you configure.
privacy.lede: aria2t runs entirely on your machine. This page lists everything it stores and every network connection it makes.
privacy.stores.intro: Everything lives under ~/.config/aria2t/ on your machine:
privacy.stores.item1: config.json — servers, theme, download directory, speed caps, seeding defaults, and scheduler rules.
privacy.stores.item2: daemon/ — the managed daemon's session, configuration, and log, so downloads resume across restarts.
privacy.stores.item3: picks.json — file selections still awaiting an answer, so the picker opens again after a restart.
privacy.stores.item4: Nothing else — no history database and no cache of downloaded content.
privacy.stores.outro: Deleting that directory removes every trace of aria2t.
privacy.network.intro: Three kinds of network traffic exist:
privacy.network.downloads.body: aria2 connects to the mirrors, trackers, and peers of the downloads you add.
privacy.network.rpc.body: aria2t talks to the aria2 server you configured — the local managed daemon or your own remote server. Nothing else.
privacy.network.site.body: aria2t.c0nn3ct.info uses Amplitude analytics to count visits. The application itself contains no analytics.
privacy.network.outro: The application makes no other connections: no update checks, no crash reports, no telemetry.
privacy.nothing.item1: No analytics or telemetry in the application.
privacy.nothing.item2: No accounts, sign-ins, or cloud services.
privacy.nothing.item3: No remote configuration or feature flags.
privacy.nothing.item4: No network traffic except to the aria2 servers you configure and the downloads you add.
